paragraphs: CampusIQ sells colleges and universities real-time space analytics meant to improve utilization, right-size facilities, and optimize occupancy. Its customers are institutions using the product for space utilization and campus planning.

Occupancy is read from the campus wireless network, so coverage scales as far as WiFi is available, with additional hardware sensors placed where it is not. Monitored spaces include classrooms, libraries, dining halls, recreation centers, residence halls, research facilities, and outdoor areas. The company says the system captures occupancy data without identifying individuals. It claims compliance with FERPA and other educational privacy regulations. Full implementation typically ranges from two to eight weeks. Field tests are reported at 95%+ accuracy in occupancy detection.

A published case study describes the University of Kentucky launching a pilot with CampusIQ in the fall of 2024. In that account, a 5% reduction in planned space translated to approximately $8M in avoided construction costs. Core pricing is based on gross square footage. Subscription models include software licensing, installation, and ongoing support.

quote.text: CampusIQ delivers real-time campus space analytics and expert insights to improve utilization, right-size facilities, and optimize space occupancy.
